title: Decision spec
description: Declarative spec for a cascaded decision: a deterministic floor, then ordered tiers, then escalate. 1.1 adds safety, thresholds, impact and per-tier timeout and acts (additive). 1.2 adds question objects (text, labels, compare) beside plain strings, and callers (additive). Rules JSON Schema cannot express (single-axis questions, pairwise questions in both orders, at most 5 labels, inline callers end at the fast tier) are `hnx decide lint`.

items.description: A plain question, or an object with its own label set. hnx decide lint requires text, at most 5 labels, and every pairwise question (compare) asked in both orders.

text.description: The question. One axis: one question mark, no 'and'/'or' joining two questions.

labels.description: The answers this question may take (at most 5, enforced by hnx decide lint).

compare.description: A pairwise question over the two named slots, written {slot} in text. Its mirror (the slots swapped) must also be in the set: asking both orders cancels position bias.

timeout_ms.description: Tier call deadline. A timeout escalates; it never answers.

acts.description: Answers from this tier are acted on without a human. The replay gate demands zero confident errors for acting tiers.

safety.description: Safety spec: model tiers may only raise the impact tier, never lower it or approve.

default_min_confidence.description: Threshold for tiers that do not set min_confidence.

callers.description: Who waits on this spec. inline: a caller blocks on the answer, so hnx decide lint requires the spec to end at the fast tier (floor, small) and then escalate, within a 1 s budget. Absent means batch only.
